ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure, a semicylinder with radius $R=0.75\mathrm{m}$ is placed on a horizontal ground. A small ball is thrown horizontally from point $B$ directly above point $A$ at the left end of the cylinder (the ball can be regarded as a particle), and it just grazes past point $C$ on the semicylinder. It is known that $O$ is the center of the semicylinder, and the angle between $O C$ and the horizontal direction is $53^{\circ}$. ($g=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$, $\sin37^{\circ}=0.6$, $\cos37^{\circ}=0.8$)

1. The time taken for the small ball to move from point $B$ to point $C$
2. The initial velocity of the small ball in projectile motion.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, a semicylinder is placed on horizontal ground, the diameter of the semicircle is on the ground, and the center of the circle is labeled O. The left endpoint is A, and point B is directly above A; a small ball is thrown from B with an initial velocity v0 horizontally to the right, and the dashed trajectory passes through and just grazes point C on the semicircular arc. In the figure, OC is a radius, and the angle between OC and the horizontal ground direction is labeled 53°. Then reason: Take O as the origin, the horizontal ground as the x-axis, and vertically upward as the y-axis. The radius R=0.75 m, so the coordinates of point A are (-R,0). Point B is directly above A, so the x-coordinate of B is -R. Point C is on the semicircle, and the angle between OC and the horizontal is 53°, so the coordinates of point C are (R cos53°, R sin53°). From sin37°=0.6 and cos37°=0.8, we can get cos53°=0.6 and sin53°=0.8. The horizontal displacement from B to C is Δx=R cos53°-(-R)=R(1+cos53°)=0.75×(1+0.6)=1.2 m. The small ball undergoes horizontal projectile motion, and the horizontal displacement satisfies v0 t=1.2. The small ball just grazes the circular arc at point C, so the velocity direction is tangent to the circular arc, and the velocity vector is perpendicular to the radius OC. The velocity at point C is (v0,-gt), and the radius direction is (R cos53°,R sin53°). The perpendicular condition is (v0,-gt)·(R cos53°,R sin53°)=0, namely v0 cos53°=gt sin53°. Therefore gt/v0=cos53°/sin53°=0.6/0.8=0.75. Also v0=1.2/t; substituting gives gt/(1.2/t)=0.75, namely gt^2/1.2=0.75. Taking g=10 m/s², we get 10t^2=0.9, t^2=0.09, so t=0.3 s. Thus v0=1.2/0.3=4 m/s. Final answer: The time from B to C is 0.3 s; the initial velocity is 4 m/s.
